exercises.name: Heavy Reverse Barbell / EZ-Bar Curl
exercises.biomechanics: Pronated forearm position wraps biceps tendon around radius, mechanically disadvantageous for biceps. Brachioradialis moment arm peaks at 90-100 deg flexion (5.0-7.5 cm). Requires static isometric contraction of ECRL/ECRB to prevent wrist collapse into flexion.
exercises.roger_c_protocol: Roger C curls 60 kg for 4 sets of 12 reps. Notes that the static extensor hold creates dense, thick wrist tendons and forearm ridges.
exercises.optimal_prescription: 3 - 4 sets of 8 - 12 reps, 2.5 min rest, strict 2-second eccentric phase.

exercises.name: Heavy Finger-Roll Barbell Wrist Curl
exercises.biomechanics: Rolling bar down to distal phalanges places FDP and FDS into extreme stretch. Initiating movement with finger flexion engages high-PCSA digit flexors (25.3 cm2 combined). FCU provides peak wrist flexion torque with 1.8 cm moment arm via pisiform sesamoid.
exercises.roger_c_protocol: Roger C works up to 50 kg wrist curls for 6 reps. Attributes the outward popping of palmar wrist tendons and massive medial forearm belly directly to this movement.
exercises.optimal_prescription: 4 sets of 10 - 15 reps, full range of motion from fingertips to full wrist flexion, 1-second pause at contraction.

exercises.name: Reverse Wrist Curl / Forearm Finisher (Wrist Extension)
exercises.biomechanics: Pure sagittal extension of carpus against gravity or cable vector. ECRB provides central line of pull. Essential for building the visible posterior 'piano strings' and counteracting hyper-toned flexors.
exercises.roger_c_protocol: Roger C recommends isolation wrist extensions or the 'Forearm Finisher' tool to create deep extensor striations and protect against wrist flexion imbalance.
exercises.optimal_prescription: 3 - 4 sets of 15 - 20 reps with light-to-moderate load or cable constant tension.

exercises.name: Arm Wrestling Strap Pronation Drill
exercises.biomechanics: Strap routes across dorsal hand into thumb crease, applying external supination torque. Pronator Teres operates at maximal mechanical leverage with elbow at 90 deg flexion.
exercises.roger_c_protocol: Roger C used 5 sets of 60 reps with 10 kg strap daily for 300+ days. Notes that high-rep tensile loading drove connective tissue, bone remodeling, and tendon thickening.
exercises.optimal_prescription: Hypertrophy mode: 3 - 4 sets of 12 - 15 reps; Tendon conditioning mode: 3 sets of 30 - 50 reps with controlled cadence.

exercises.name: Rising / Radial Deviation Strap Drill
exercises.biomechanics: Applies downward ulnar deviation torque across the index knuckle. ECRL and ECRB fire to elevate the wrist vertically in neutral plane, thickening the radial styloid region.
exercises.roger_c_protocol: Roger C paired 5 sets of 60 reps rising with pronation daily. Emphasizes that this movement attacks the joint structure and radial tendon insertion directly.
exercises.optimal_prescription: 3 - 4 sets of 15 - 20 reps or loaded static holds with judo belt/strap.

exercises.name: Resisted Supination (Antagonist Balancer)
exercises.biomechanics: Isolates the deep supinator muscle. Crucial antagonist to Pronator Teres to prevent medial epicondylitis (golfer's elbow) and restore normal radioulnar arthrokinematics.
exercises.roger_c_protocol: Roger C admits completely ignoring supination for months, resulting in severe elbow pain. Added band supination to eliminate pain and restore hook capability.
exercises.optimal_prescription: 2 - 3 sets of 15 - 20 reps with elastic band or offset dumbbell 2-3x per week.

exercises.name: Ulnar Deviation Levering (Antagonist Balancer)
exercises.biomechanics: Antagonist movement to rising. Clamps FCU and ECU synchronously, stabilizing the triangular fibrocartilage complex (TFCC) on the ulnar side of the wrist.
exercises.roger_c_protocol: Prescribed alongside supination to counter the 60-rep rising drills and balance the wrist circumference symmetrically.
exercises.optimal_prescription: 2 - 3 sets of 15 - 20 reps with light lever or band.

exercises.name: Axle / Fat Grip Dead Hangs & Holds
exercises.biomechanics: Large diameter (2 to 2.5 inches) forces hand open, preventing passive mechanical finger locking. Requires continuous maximal voluntary contraction of FDP and FDS muscle bellies.
exercises.roger_c_protocol: Recommends fat grips on dumbbells and barbells as an essential base for hand and wrist adaptation.
exercises.optimal_prescription: 3 - 4 sets of 20 - 40 second holds to near failure.
